claude.sample_unit: questions (100 adversarial attack questions plus 36 legitimate questions)
models_evaluated: GPT-4o-mini direct prompting with raw IC document

links.outcome: Appropriate refusal of adversarial/out-of-scope questions and utility on legitimate questions, with vs without OOD classifier
links.effect: OOD classifier raised appropriate refusal from 0.94 to 0.97 but cut utility from 0.86 to 0.69; RESPECT 0.97 refusal vs direct prompting 0.90 (p<0.05); direct prompting utility 1.00.
links.quote: Adding the OOD classifier improved appropriate refusal from 0.94 to 0.97, though at the cost of reduced utility (0.86 to 0.69).

links.outcome: Whether the conversational AI declines out-of-scope/inappropriate questions in adversarial simulation
links.effect: RESPECT appropriate refusal 0.97 vs Direct Prompting 0.90 (p<0.05); utility 0.69 vs 1.00. Single-turn questions only, not multi-turn.
links.quote: RESPECT achieved an appropriate refusal rate of 0.97 and utility of 0.69, significantly outperforming Direct Prompting in appropriate refusal (0.90, p < 0.05) while Direct Prompting achieved perfect utility (1.00, p < 0.05).

links.outcome: Retrieval and generation accuracy of RAG grounded in curated Q/A knowledge base vs random retrieval and direct prompting
links.effect: RESPECT outperformed Random RAG on all metrics (e.g., LLM-judge 0.49 vs 0.15 in leave-one-out), but direct prompting with raw document scored higher on generation (0.94 vs 0.49).
links.quote: RESPECT outperforms Random RAG across both retrieval and generation, demonstrating that the system can identify relevant information from its knowledge base even when queries are outside of the sample.

links.outcome: Accuracy under paraphrased queries with misspellings and colloquialisms
links.effect: On rephrased queries RESPECT scored above Random RAG on all metrics (faithfulness 0.70, LLM-judge 0.71), higher than in leave-one-out; direct prompting still higher on generation (0.90).
links.quote: Here, we note that the generation scores are higher than in the cross-validation analysis, since the system is more likely to answer a query.

openai.sample_unit: questions (100 adversarial attack questions and 36 legitimate questions)

links.effect: OOD classifier improved appropriate refusal 0.94 to 0.97 but reduced utility 0.86 to 0.69; RESPECT RUC-AUC 0.81.
links.quote: Adding the OOD classifier improved appropriate refusal from 0.94 to 0.97, though at the cost of reduced utility (0.86 to 0.69).

links.effect: Rephrasing: RESPECT vs Random RAG faithfulness 0.70 vs 0.24, factual correctness 0.59 vs 0.16, LLM-judge 0.71 vs 0.32; Direct prompting LLM-judge 0.90.
links.quote: Again, RESPECT outperforms Random RAG across all retrieval and generation metrics.

links.effect: LOOCV: RESPECT vs Random RAG faithfulness 0.58 vs 0.14, factual correctness 0.28 vs 0.07, LLM-judge generation 0.49 vs 0.15; Direct prompting LLM-judge 0.94.
links.quote: RESPECT outperforms Random RAG across both retrieval and generation, demonstrating that the system can identify relevant information from its knowledge base even when queries are outside of the sample.
